items.title: 검사 퇴직자 올해도 110명…5년째 100명 넘었다
items.summary: 올해 들어 9월 말까지 법복을 벗은 검사가 110명으로 집계됐다. 이로써 연간 퇴직 검사는 5년 연속 100명을 넘어섰다. 검사들의 이탈이 이어지면서 전국 검찰청 미제 사건은 9월 말 기준 18만6307건으로 늘었다.13일 법무부에 따르면 올해 초부터 9월 말까지 퇴직 검사는 누적 110명이다. 현행 검사정원법상 정원 2292명의 4.7%, 8월 기준 검사 현원 2129명의 5.2%에 해당한다. 서울중앙지방공소청에 근무하는 검사 200여 명의 절반 가량이고, 규모가 상대적으로 작은 지방공소청 전체 검사 인원을 웃도는 숫자다.연간 퇴직 검사 수는 2018년까지 70∼80명 선이었다가 검경 수사권 조정을 앞둔 2019년 111명으로 급증했고, 이후 다시 100명 미만으로 줄었다. 검경 수사권 조정으로 검찰 수사권이 대폭 축소된 직후인 2022년에는 146명으로 다시 늘었고, 2023년 145명, 2024년 132명으로 매년 100명을 훌쩍 넘겼다. 이재명 정부가 출범하고 검찰청 폐지

items.title: 단국대 경영대학원, ESG 심사 전문인력 키운다
items.summary: 단국대 경영대학원은 (사)국제ESG심사원협회와 ESG 전문인력 양성을 위한 업무협약을 맺었다고 13일 밝혔다. 협약식은 지난 8일 단국대 죽전캠퍼스에서 정연승 경영대학원장과 김영국 협회장 등이 참석한 가운데 열렸다. 두 기관은 이번 협약으로 교육·연구개발 사업 공동 참여, ESG 실무 전문가 양성 프로그램 공동 운영, 정보 공유와 인적 교류 등에 협력한다. 협회 회원이 단국대 경영대학원에 진학할 경우 장학 혜택도 지원하기로 했다. 경영대학원은 ESG경영전공 석사과정과 연계해 현장 중심 교육과정을 보강하고, 협회 회원에게 학위 취득과 공동 연구 기회를 제공할 계획이다. 정 원장은 “심사·평가 전문 네트워크를 갖춘 협회와 손잡고 산업 현장에 필요한 지속가능경영 리더를 길러내겠다”고 말했다. 김 협회장은 “기업의 지속가능성은 ESG 평가와 심사의 신뢰성에서 출발한다”며 “이론과 실무를 겸비한 심사 전문인력을 체계적으로 양성하겠다”고 했다.

items.title: As a scientist, here's what worries me about the suspected Russian plague victim | Devi Sridhar
items.summary: Russia’s silence over the death of a lab worker underlines that pandemic preparedness amounts to nothing if information on threats is withheld In pandemic preparedness work, scientists like to focus on the technical challenges: identifying pathogens, diagnosing infections, understanding their effects and developing vaccines and treatments. Each step promises progress through human innovation, investment and planning. The World Health Organization (WHO), for example, brings experts together to identify and prioritise emerging disease threats and collect the evidence needed to prepare for them. But preparedness depends on more than scientific innovation. As the past week has shown, politics is the elephant in the room in all of this. No one could have predicted we would be talking about pneumonic plague, and that the death of a single lab worker in Russia would cause global headlines. It might feel like an overreaction: the WHO deals with thousands of potential disease signals worldwide every month. But the circumstances of this case are unusual given the lack of transparency from Russian authorities on what happened – and ongoing concern about biological weapons research. Continue reading...

items.summary: Aberffraw, Ynys Môn (Anglesey): Plenty of fungi can be found among the sand here; in fact it is vital to keeping the dunes at bay Dapperlings and toughshanks, bonnets and brittlegills, bird’s nests and fairy clubs. Fungi season has begun, and for me it is heralded by the “fungus foray” held at Bangor University’s Treborth Botanic Garden. An annual event, this year it produced more than 200 species in just 90 minutes, thanks to the 225 forayers who took part. Among the feast of colour and form was one I’d never seen in 50 years of foraying – orange ping‑pong bat fungus (Favolaschia calocera), glowing vivid along a fallen twig. articles.title: 단국대 경영대학원, ESG 심사 전문인력 키운다
articles.snippet: 단국대 경영대학원은 (사)국제ESG심사원협회와 ESG 전문인력 양성을 위한 업무협약을 맺었다고 13일 밝혔다. 협약식은 지난 8일 단국대 죽전캠퍼스에서 정연승 경영대학원장과 김영국 협회장 등이 참석한 가운데 열렸다. 두 기관은 이번 협약으로 교육·연구개발 사업 공동 참여, ESG 실무 전문가 양성 프로그램 공동 운영, 정보 공유와 인적 교류 등에 협력한다. 협회 회원이 단국대 경영대학원에 진학할 경우 장학 혜택도 지원하기로 했다. 경영대학원은 ESG경영전공 석사과정과 연계해 현장 중심 교육과정을 보강하고, 협회 회원에게 학위 취득과 공동 연구 기회를 제공할 계획이다. 정 원장은 “심사·평가 전문 네트워크를 갖춘 협회와 손잡고 산업 현장에 필요한 지속가능경영 리더를 길러내겠다”고 말했다. 김 협회장은 “기업의 지속가능성은 ESG 평가와 심사의 신뢰성에서 출발한다”며 “이론과 실무를 겸비한 심사 전문인력을 체계적으로 양성하겠다”고 했다.

articles.snippet: Warning: contains spoilers The four short scenes added to the new version has made the film the highest-grossing of all time – but the only people really enjoying this are the Disney accountants Does it really matter which film is the highest-grossing of all time at the global box office? Will James Cameron be lying awake at night staring into the darkness and pondering whether to withdraw humanity’s access to giant, blue-skinned space elves out of sheer spite, just because Avatar has been dethroned once again by Avengers: Endgame? It seems unlikely. Are the Russo brothers at this very moment leaping and capering with wild abandon because adding a few new scenes and releasing their film for the umpteenth time has led to this momentous changing of the guard? Probably not. Is a Disney accountant somewhere holding a tiny awards ceremony in which every nominee is himself? Well yes, absolutely, because the mouse house ultimately owns both films. And yet the most interesting thing about Avengers: Endgame’s return to cinemas is not how much money it has made – for the record, the rerelease, titled Avengers Endgame: Encore, had brought in another $126m worldwide by last weekend, taking its lifetime total to approximately $2.925bn (just ahead of Avatar’s $2.923bn) – but what Marvel added to the picture while we were all busy counting. articles.snippet: Genden Phuntsok brings charm and innocence to his portrayal of Tenzing Norgay, while Tom Hiddleston is suitably frank as Edmund Hillary Here is a well intentioned, watchable, if sometimes soft-edged film with some NatGeo production values on high mountain peaks. The subject is the triumphant Mount Everest expedition of 1953, in which the ultimate ascent was achieved by Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay and New Zealander Edmund Hillary. Tenzing, a former guide whose unparalleled knowledge of the mountain and exemplary climbing skills earned him promotion to full team member, is played here by Tibetan actor Genden Phuntsok, while Hillary is robustly portrayed by Tom Hiddleston. Screenwriter Luke Davies and director Jennifer Peedom have the decent aim of restoring Tenzing’s achievement to the centre of the narrative, a tale which at the time was resoundingly claimed for Hillary and the British empire: a glorious redemption of Scott’s Antarctic ordeal 41 years earlier and a sign of divine approval for the imminent coronation of Queen Elizabeth II. articles.title: ‘Sometimes she publishes notes she’s scribbled on her hand’: Édouard Louis on 10 reasons to love Anne Carson
articles.snippet: The French author discovered Carson on a bus while stranded in a snowstorm and has been enthralled by her fearless imagination ever since Where to start with Anne Carson ‘Delights await!’: Margaret Atwood and other writers on Nobel winner Anne Carson 1. Anne Carson is one of the greatest writers of our time. I discovered her work on a Peter Pan bus from New York to New England. I’d bought Antigonick in a bookstore a few days earlier, almost randomly. From the very first lines, I was enthralled. While we were on the bus, a snowstorm suddenly blanketed the roads, and the other passengers and I found ourselves stuck for 10 hours in rural America, surrounded by an entirely white landscape. I took my computer out of my backpack and started to translate Antigonick into French. Spontaneously. I was so absorbed by the power of Carson’s text that I didn’t notice the hours pass. 2. One of Carson’s greatest strengths is that, unlike so many other contemporary writers, she doesn’t try to “make literature”. She writes. Sometimes clouds do the speaking, in her work, and sometimes monsters do; sometimes, in the middle of a collection of poems, she lets an imaginary Catherine Deneuve take over the narration. Sometimes she writes a letter to her own sleep and sometimes she publishes notes she’s scribbled on her hand. She writes about Homer, but also Rosalía; about Brecht, but also Marilyn Monroe. articles.title: Winning the Nobel prize in literature only underlines Anne Carson’s infinite genius | Yiyun Li
articles.snippet: When her sons died the Book of Goose author turned to Grief Lessons, Carson’s translation of four plays by Euripides. She reflects on the ‘life sustaining’ work of an extraordinary writer • Where to start with: Anne Carson • ‘Delights await!’: Margaret Atwood and other writers on Anne Carson It is preposterous to agree to write a short piece on Anne Carson’s work. The task is impossible, akin to that of solving the mathematical problem of dividing zero by zero. If one had the power to solve it, perhaps one would have some confidence in attempting to write about Anne Carson’s work. Attempting, I say, not succeeding. In attempting to do so, I shall emphasise that all words fall short in extreme situations, which not only include unfathomable losses (of children, in my case) but also include articulating anything about Anne Carson’s work. One could start with Carson’s words. “Words, if you let them, will do what they want to do and what they have to do.” (Autobiography of Red) But to let the words exist in their own desires and yearnings and frustrations and confusions, to let the words scream with inarticulable pain or tell a riddle with a twinkling smile or make love to one another – how many of us have achieved that kind of mastery of words? But, oh no, mastery is the wrong word here. Only the minor and the greedy and the power-thirsty writers want to be the masters of the words. Carson does not subjugate or manipulate her words. She lets them be; and lets herself be led by the words – hers, and the ancients’ translated into unforgettable English by her. Continue reading...
